_comment: Rules of the Player's Handbook (2024): the Rules Glossary, the rules sections of chapters 1, 2, 6 and 7 and Appendix A; and the Dungeon Master's Guide (2024): the sections of its chapters, the DM's Toolbox systems and the parts left out (EXPANSIONS.md section 1.3). Names, pages and classification only.

entries.name: Alignment
entries.note: Kept as a stat block and sentient item field (and on the planes, Expansion 26); there is no alignment system for the player (section 1.3).

entries.name: High Jump
entries.note: adapted: only the long jump is used on the battle mat; a high jump would only reach a flier, and the mat counts a flier's height in reach already

entries.name: Telepathy
entries.note: adapted: kept on every stat block with its range; no creature of this expansion has it, and Influence in a fight does not yet ask for a shared language (it will when languages matter)

Covers: Know Your Players, Group Size, Multiple DMs, Narration, Improvising Answers, Roleplaying, Using a Map, Tracking Initiative, Tracking Monsters' Hit Points, Using and Tracking Conditions, Tracking Position at Long Range, Narration in Combat, Keeping Combat Moving, Adjusting Difficulty.

entries.name: Starting Attitude
entries.note: by the leader's alignment, weighted towards Hostile for bands met as trouble

entries.note: Section 1.3: the DMG's tools for the DM's own creations are used as guidance whenever Realmwalker invents something of its own.

entries.name: Environmental Effects
entries.note: Its planar effects are in world.json (Expansion 26).

entries.name: Firearms and Explosives
entries.note: Renaissance items only, as rare gnomish inventions; the modern and futuristic ones are left out (section 1.3).

entries.name: Alien Technology
entries.note: Section 1.3: the DMG's modern and futuristic weapons and its alien technology break the setting.

entries.name: Gods and Other Powers
entries.note: The named gods of the multiverse are not transplanted; each world has its own faiths (section 1.3).

entries.name: Adjudicating Areas of Effect
entries.note: Printed in Mobs: how many targets an area catches without a grid.

entries.name: Nonplayer Characters
entries.note: Nonplayer characters and attitudes in depth (Appendix E).

entries.name: Settlements
entries.note: Its traits and calamities are in world.json.

entries.name: Supernatural Gifts
entries.note: Its blessings and charms are in world.json.

entries.name: Chapter 4: Creating Adventures (DM advice)
entries.note: Section 1.3: DM advice, used as design guidance, not as content. Covers: Step-by-Step Adventures, Lay Out the Premise, Adventure Premise, Adventure Conflict, Adventure Situations by Level, Adventure Setting, Draw In the Players, Adventure Patrons, Supernatural Hooks, Happenstance Hooks, Plan Encounters, Character Objectives, Keeping the Adventure Moving, Something for Everyone, Multiple Ways to Progress, Social Interaction Encounters, Exploration Encounters, Encounter Pace and Tension, Bring It to an End, Denouement, Adventure Examples.

entries.name: Combat Encounters
entries.note: bands are built for the land's danger (a party level), not the party; the budget trims a band, never past the last of a kind, and a lone traveller still meets fewer of the rank and file (Fair Chances)

entries.name: Monster Behavior
entries.note: Initial attitudes (Appendix E); the rest is guidance for the enemy's tactics (section 4.7).

entries.name: Random Encounters
entries.note: the game's own encounter tables by land, danger and hour, sized by the XP budget

entries.name: Treasure Hoards
entries.note: CR 11-16 money: the book prints 8d8 x 10,000 with an average of 36,000; the average is kept (x 1,000)

entries.name: Quest Rewards
entries.note: the giver pays the coin the terms say (a village cannot pay a hoard); for great works a lord, priest or headman adds the hoard row's magic items

entries.name: Chapter 5: Creating Campaigns
entries.note: Section 1.3: DM advice, used as design guidance, not as content.

entries.name: Greyhawk
entries.note: Section 1.3: Greyhawk is not transplanted; Realmwalker's worlds are generated and have their own faiths.

entries.name: Other Configurations
entries.note: Expansion 26 chooses how Realmwalker's planes are arranged.

entries.name: Alignment and the Outer Planes
entries.note: Alignment matters on the planes (section 1.3); Planar Dissonance is in world.json.

entries.name: Spells
entries.note: The spells that reach other planes, under Planar Travel.

entries.name: Traveling the Outer Planes
entries.note: Its four crossings are in world.json.

entries.name: Planar Adventure Situations
entries.note: Section 1.3: DM advice, used as design guidance, not as content.

entries.name: Tour of the Multiverse
entries.note: Each plane has its own entry in world.json.

entries.name: Art Objects
entries.note: the objects are named in the game's own words, keeping each table's value

entries.name: Magic Item Categories
entries.note: the game's own item kinds (weapon, armour, shield, jewellery, clothing, focus, potions, scrolls) stand for the nine categories until the named items arrive

entries.name: Awarding Magic Items
entries.note: the Magic Item Rarities table is read by the hoard's CR, since enemies scale with the land and not the party; the tracker sheet is the DM's and is not used

entries.name: Magic Items for Starting Characters
entries.note: With starting at higher levels (Expansion 14), by theme.

entries.name: Consumable Items
entries.note: Consumable items (Appendix E).

entries.name: Magic Item Special Features
entries.note: each item's maker, history and look come from the world's own past (names, places, years) instead of the d20 tables

entries.name: Appendix A: Lore Glossary
entries.note: Section 1.3: the Lore Glossary is not transplanted; Realmwalker's worlds are generated and have their own faiths.

entries.name: Appendix B: Maps
entries.note: Section 1.3: the maps are not copied; they are archetypes for new site and dungeon styles.

entries.name: Tracking Sheets
entries.note: Section 1.3: DM advice, used as design guidance, not as content. The game keeps its own records (journal, ledgers).
